signals.title_or_quote: Auto-clipping: turn a long video or stream into short clips
signals.why_relevant: User wants to auto-clip long videos into shorts, matching podclip's core function.
signals.drafted_reply: One approach is to use transcript-driven heuristics first—like preferring sentence boundaries and high speech density—before adding AI. This gives a testable baseline. I built a tool that does this for podcasts—{APP_URL}. I'm the creator.

rescore.why: The thread is a GitHub issue requesting open-source contributors to build an auto-clipping feature inside an existing codebase, not a podcaster or creator looking for a ready-made clipping tool.

signals.why_relevant: They're building highlight detection for podcasts, which is exactly what podclip does.
signals.drafted_reply: For scoring highlights, combining transcript sentiment, keyword density, and audio energy works well. Our model was trained on 40k rated clips to avoid generic picks. More here: {APP_URL}. I'm the founder.

rescore.why: The thread is a GitHub epic tracking active open-source development of a custom scoring and highlight-detection pipeline — the author is building this infrastructure themselves, not looking for a finished product to replace that work.

signals.title_or_quote: I frequently find myself wanting to share information surfaced in a podcast... but I don't have a great way of sharing.
signals.why_relevant: User struggles to share podcast snippets, a core use case for podclip.
signals.drafted_reply: You could use a tool that auto-detects strong moments and exports them with captions. I built one that picks narrative hooks, not random clips—{APP_URL}. I'm the creator.

rescore.why: HN thread locked (older than 14 days) — cannot reply

signals.why_relevant: They're building a professional clipping studio, directly overlapping with podclip's ICP.
signals.drafted_reply: Local, reliable clipping with full control is key for pros. We focused on speed and brand consistency—rendering a 60-min episode in ~90 seconds. Check it out: {APP_URL}. I'm the builder.

rescore.why: The thread is a GitHub issue tracking a local-first, privacy-preserving, Rust-based clipping tool being built by the author themselves — they are building a competitor, not looking for an existing SaaS solution like podclip.

signals.title_or_quote: Feature: Implement Chapter Support with Navigation
signals.why_relevant: Chapter support implies need for clip-level navigation, adjacent to podclip's use case.
signals.drafted_reply: Chapter data can also feed clip detection—moments right after chapter starts often have strong intros. Our tool auto-generates clips with captions: {APP_URL}. I'm the creator.

rescore.why: This thread is a GitHub feature request for implementing chapter navigation (ID3 tags, MP4 metadata, RSS parsing) in a podcast player app — a developer task unrelated to automated clip generation for social media.
